review_notes: I read the whole target file, the underlying AffineEquiv.ofEq and affineSubspaceMap API in LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace, and the simp API of ContinuousAffineEquiv (refl, symm, toAffineEquiv_symm). I did not run Lean. The finding is about missing simp lemmas. The `subtypeA` lemmas and `affineSubspaceMap_apply` look fine. The simp lemma `affineSubspaceMap_apply_symm_apply` has a LHS that is already in normal form, so I did not report it.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem coe_ofEq_apply {s t : AffineSubspace R P} [Nonempty s] [Nonempty t]
    (h : s = t) (x : s) : (ofEq h x : P) = x := AffineEquiv.coe_ofEq_apply s t h x
findings.problem: The non-continuous `AffineEquiv.ofEq` has simp lemmas `ofEq_symm` (symm of ofEq is ofEq of h.symm) and `ofEq_rfl` (ofEq of rfl is refl). The continuous `ofEq` here gets only `coe_ofEq_apply`. So a term like `(ofEq h).symm` or `ofEq rfl` has no simp normal form. Simp cannot rewrite `(ofEq h).symm` to `ofEq h.symm`, and it cannot rewrite `ofEq rfl` to `ContinuousAffineEquiv.refl`. Here `ContinuousAffineEquiv.refl` already has `coe_refl` and `refl_apply` as simp lemmas. The `ofEq` definition is also not unfolded by simp. So the coercion lemma is the only available rule, and expressions containing `.symm` of `ofEq` or `ofEq rfl` stay stuck, even though the underlying AffineEquiv versions already normalize.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem ofEq_symm (h : s = t) : (ofEq h).symm = ofEq h.symm` and `@[simp] theorem ofEq_rfl : ofEq (rfl : s = s) = ContinuousAffineEquiv.refl R s`. Both can be proved by `ext; rfl`, using `ContinuousAffineEquiv.ext`. Optionally also add a `toAffineEquiv_ofEq` lemma, so that the bridge to `AffineEquiv.ofEq` can be simp-rewritten.
findings.benefit: This matches the simp interface of the underlying `AffineSubspace.ofEq` in the affine setting (`ofEq_symm`, `ofEq_rfl`). It gives `.symm` and `rfl` instances a canonical normal form, so users do not have to add `ext` and `rfl` steps by hand.

evidence.excerpt: theorem ofEq_symm (h : S₁ = S₂) : (ofEq S₁ S₂ h).symm = ofEq S₂ S₁ h.symm
theorem ofEq_rfl : ofEq S₁ S₁ rfl = AffineEquiv.refl k S₁ := rfl
theorem refl_apply (x : P₁) : refl k P₁ x = x
